summary: Elevated TTFB for chat completions after runtime/model upgrade - customer reports increased first-token latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NimbleDocs) reports a sharp increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions immediately after a scheduled runtime + model variant upgrade rolled out to their Dedicated fleet in us-east-1. The regressions began after the 2024-11-04 runtime deployment that included kernel selection changes and a new quantized execution path for redwood-chat-v2.

Impact:
- Multiple chat completion requests now exhibit first-token latency in the 600-1200ms range (previous baseline ~120-250ms).
- Increased request timeout incidents observed in customer app (they have a 1s client-level timeout).
- Customer-facing errors: perceived application sluggishness and occasional 504s.

Environment:
- Customer dedicated capacity in us-east-1.
- Runtime version: rtd-2024.11.04+kernel-opt (deployed 2024-11-04 02:10 UTC)
- Serving config: model pin redwood-chat-v2@v2.3.1, fallback chain includes gptx-open-13b@q4_0.

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer and validated):
1) Send a chat completion request with typical prompt size (~200 tokens history) to customer route.
2) Observe server response start time vs request arrival; TTFB measured at server-side and client-side.
3) Repeat across 10-20 requests to see variability and spikes.

Observed behavior:
- Median TTFB increased to ~650ms; 95th percentile >1.1s.
- Token-streaming starts delayed even on cold and warm KV cache hits.
- CPU utilization on serving nodes remains within normal range; GPU utilization shows intermittent dips during spikes.
- Some requests fall back to gptx-open-13b but still show elevated TTFB.

Expected behavior:
- Median TTFB approximately 120-250ms for same traffic profile and model pin.
- Stable streaming start across warm cache conditions.

Logs / traces / metrics attached:
- Attached traces: nimbledocs_trace_20241105_14z.jsonl (sampled spans showing blocking in compilation/kernal selection phase).
- Serving runtime logs: runtime_node-12_2024-11-05.log (corresponding timestamps showing extended kernel selection time).
- Customer-provided client logs showing request timeouts and retry behavior.

Customer impact and urgency:
- Customer reports production impact causing support escalation. They are on a dedicated plan with committed SLAs; they require mitigation within 48 hours or a rollback.

Workarounds tried by customer and support:
- Customer temporarily increased client timeout to 3s (mitigates timeouts but not the latency).
- Support recommended pinning to previous model variant (redwood-chat-v2@v2.3.0) — customer requested Redwood assist with migration/rollback.

Attachments:
- nimbledocs_trace_20241105_14z.jsonl
- runtime_node-12_2024-11-05.log

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: kernel-selection/compilation checks introduced extra blocking on CPU threadpool during request startup for quantized execution paths.
Correlation observed between TTFB spikes and log entries: "kernel_selector: checking kernels for q4 pathways" with 300-900ms durations.
GPU metrics: intermittent underutilization during spikes -> suggests CPU-side decision path delaying GPU dispatch rather than GPU saturation.
A/B test in staging toggling 'skip_kernel_verification_on_warm_cache' flag reduced median TTFB from 620ms to 185ms for same request set.
No evidence of network/NLB issues for this customer; TLS handshake and proxy latency normal in traces.
Fallback to gptx-open-13b shows elevated TTFB too, indicating shared decision-path code affected multiple model variants.
Related prior tickets: SUP-27450 documented similar post-upgrade latency spike for a different customer in eu-west; root cause there pointed to same kernel-selection change.
resolution_notes: Mitigation scheduled: rollout of runtime patch rtd-2024.11.07 that short-circuits kernel verification on warm cache nodes and defers expensive checks to background async path.
Temporary action: Support to coordinate pinning NimbleDocs fleet to redwood-chat-v2@v2.3.0 if they prefer immediate rollback. Customer opted for coordinated patch deployment first.
Post-deploy verification plan: monitor TTFB dashboards (per-route) for 24h, sample traces from 5 customer routes, and confirm error/timeout rates return to baseline.
Follow-up: Engineering to add targeted perf unit tests for kernel selection path and add a canary gating metric for future runtime upgrades.
Status: patch queued for deployment 2024-11-07 18:30 UTC; awaiting change window confirmation from infra team.
notes: Owner: Riley Chen (SRE). Engineering lead: Priya Malhotra. Keep customer updated hourly until mitigation completed.
